newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp says no guarantees on Dortmund plant.
newsitem.headline: Krupp says no guarantees on Dortmund plant.

text.p: German steel maker Krupp will make no guarantees not to close its Dortmund plant, the company said in a statement.
Earlier reports that Krupp personnel director Juergen Rossberg had guaranteed not to close at least part of the Dortmund plant quoted him out of context, the company said.
What Rossberg actually said was that the blast furnace and steel works would not be closed "unilaterally without an appropriate trade-off," the company said.
Neither Krupp nor Rossberg commented on Krupp's hot rolling mill also located in Dortmund.

Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch Krupp began talks on Thursday with its larger rival Thyssen AG aimed at merging their steel operations. The talks are an attempt by Thyssen and the state government to forestall a hostile takeover bid by Krupp.
Rossberg said that in the event of a merger, the negative consequences such as job cuts must be shared fairly between the two companies.
Analysts have speculated Krupp's Dortmund works would be the most likely target for rationalisation in the event of a merger, as the Krupp plant is less modern than Thyssen facilities.
The management board of Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp believes it will take at least six months to work out a viable plan for a fusion of the two companies' steel operations, Rossberg said.
